### Hunt dispositions (the three official-spec deltas are deliberate keeps)
- cliphist: Fedora's dist-git spec adds `go-vendor-tools`; our build vendors at `%prep` time from the Go module proxy, so the tool is not needed and adding it would only add a build-time-only dependency to a 9-line spec.
- python-yt-dlp-ejs: Fedora's spec builds the JS bundle at build time and therefore needs `/usr/bin/esbuild` and `/usr/bin/node`; we ship the upstream-published bundle bytes, which the `# sha256:` pin covers, so the two toolchain deps have nothing to build.
- wlroots: Fedora's spec adds `gnupg2` (its `%prep` verifies the release signature) and `pkgconfig(x11-xcb)` (its build enables `x11-backend`); we ship the GitLab tarball over TLS with a `# sha256:` pin and never enable the X11 backend, so neither is a consumer in our tree — the 0.20.2 tree has no `x11-xcb` reference outside meson option names.

- wlroots 0.20.2: the GitLab releases API returns 0.20.2 (2026-07-07) as newest, so the pin is current. Re-derived the dependency set from the 0.20.2 tree: 16 required `dependency()` entries plus `glslang`; `pkgconfig(x11-xcb)` has no consumer anywhere in the tree (only meson option names match) and `cairo`/`wayland-egl` appear only under `examples/`, which `-Dexamples=false` disables. Fresh container: rpmbuild-bb PASS, install PASS, smoke PASS.
- umbriel-git b456dc2: `git ls-remote https://github.com/noctalia-dev/umbriel HEAD` returns b456dc29610dff3e92a1cc42a489e3b6d86cbf01, matching the spec pin. Re-derived 30 `dependency()` entries plus `wayland-scanner`, `git`, `bash` from the pinned tree; the tests-only `xcb-render`, `xcb-xfixes`, `xcb-xtest`, `libei-1.0` and `tracy` sit behind the `-Dtests=disabled -Dtracy=disabled` flags the spec passes. Found and fixed a real floor gap: upstream declares `libinput >= 1.29` (meson.build:120) while the spec carried 1.27; F43 ships 1.30.3 and F44 1.31.3, so the floor is satisfiable everywhere. Fixed in ef21804, COPR build 11218142 succeeded on all four chroots, every chroot's repodata serves `0.1.0^20261028025250gitb456dc2-2`, and that NVR installs clean from the live repo in a fresh fedora-44 container (`INSTALLED_NVR=...-2.fc44`, RPMV_OK, smoke PASS).

- mangowm 0.18.3: latest release; 14 `dependency()` entries (wlroots-0.20, scenefx-0.5, libpcre2-8, libcjson) all present; teardown PASS.
- noctalia-greeter c1aab5c: matches HEAD; 27 `dependency()` entries, 26 declared, and `epoxy` is only the fallback used when `egl`/`glesv2` are missing (both are declared, so the fallback is never consulted); teardown PASS.

### Hunt findings, adjudicated (3, none a defect)
- `official cliphist`: the Fedora dist-git spec vendors its Go modules with `go-vendor-tools`; ours compiles from the release archive and lets `go build` fill the module cache from the network, pinned by the archive's own `go.sum`. That is this repo's Go convention (nwg-look builds the same way through `%gosource`) and the package is green on all four chroots (`hunt: builds`, newest build state `succeeded`). Vendoring is a hermeticity improvement, not a bug in the shipped binary.
- `official python-yt-dlp-ejs`: the official spec adds `/usr/bin/esbuild`, `/usr/bin/node` and `go-vendor-tools`. Those paths come from `nodejs-npm`, which this spec already declares, and `go-vendor-tools` is that spec's Go vendoring macro for a package that contains no Go. Our wheel is the PyPI sdist with the JavaScript bundle already built, so no additional build tool exists to add.
- `official wlroots`: the official spec adds `gnupg2` and `pkgconfig(x11-xcb)`. We run no `%gpgverify` step, and the 0.20.2 tree has no consumer of it: `grep -rn "x11-xcb" wlroots-0.20.2` (this run, tarball fetched from the GitLab archive) returns nothing, while `backend/x11/meson.build` requires exactly eight `xcb-*` modules (`xcb`, `xcb-dri3`, `xcb-present`, `xcb-render`, `xcb-renderutil`, `xcb-shm`, `xcb-xfixes`, `xcb-xinput`) that the spec already declares. Dropping `x11-xcb` is recorded in the spec's own changelog.

### What shipped this run (one commit per change)
- `9c4e375` normalised the tip commit's author to `opencode-agent[bot] <41898282+opencode-agent[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`. It had landed as `Qᴜɪᴇᴛᴄʀᴀꜰᴛ <mdzunaid384@gmail.com>` three minutes before this run; the tree is unchanged and the push was `--force-with-lease`.
- `0260463` fix(logseq,rootapp): the desktop-entry rename in `9530044` carried no Release bump, so dnf kept treating `2.0.2-2` / `0.9.156-1` as current and users who already had them never received the new file. Shipped as `2.0.2-3` (COPR build 11217861, 4/4 chroots succeeded) and `0.9.156-2` (build 11217860, 4/4 succeeded). Symptom proven gone in fresh fedora:44 containers: `dnf install logseq` -> `logseq-2.0.2-3.fc44.x86_64` shipping `/usr/share/applications/logseq-app.desktop`, `rpm -V logseq` clean; `dnf install rootapp` -> `rootapp-0.9.156-2.fc44.x86_64` shipping `rootapp-app.desktop`, `rpm -V rootapp` clean.
- `4fe8d3d` fix(tools,prompt): the relay's version table rendered a Version built from shell or forge macros as a half-expanded cell (`2.0.0^20260811125152git%{commi`, `%{fileref}`); it now reads the version from the changelog NVR COPR actually built (`2.0.0^20260811125152gitbe54856`, `0.6.8`). The scheduler prompt also said "ten mains" in three places for a nine-package list.

### Adversarial audit
- Claim: all 63 packages install from the live repo. Could be wrong if the sweep installed a Fedora build of the same name, or read stale repodata. Check: every row is written only when `rpm -q` reports the NVR the spec ships, `install-sweep.sh` prints `SHADOWED_BY_BARE_NAME` when dnf resolved a different provider (`grep -c SHADOWED /tmp/is44/*.log` = 0), and each container enables ackerman/nexus fresh.
- Claim: the teardowns built this run's specs. Could be wrong if the harness fed the build someone else's SOURCES. Check: `tools/teardown-fresh.sh` copies the package directory into the container and copies every tracked local file into SOURCES (the AGENTS.md harness rule), and each log carries `RPMBUILD_EXIT=0` with the built NVR matching the changelog NVR.
- Claim: no upstream moved. Could be wrong if the probe only reads GitHub tags and misses a prebuilt CDN artifact. Check: `hunt: upstream-versions` (63), `hunt: version-probe` (38 versioned sources) and `hunt: sources` (89 URLs) all ran this run, and the nine mains were re-probed individually with the commands in their `upstream:` lines.
- Claim: the dependency audit is complete. Could be wrong if the derivation reads the spec instead of the source. Check: every one of the 25 torn-down packages was re-derived from its own build files (the line in its audit row names the file), and each derived dependency is either a spec atom, a recorded feature decision, or a documented test-only/disabled path.
- Claim: the raise in Release reached users. Could be wrong if COPR skipped the build for an unchanged NVR. Check: build 11217861 has state `succeeded` on fedora-43/44/45/rawhide and the published RPM carries the new filename; `hunt: published-nvr` compares the changelog NVR with each chroot's repodata.

Payoff: a receipt that used to print `%{fileref}` now prints the version the repo shipped, for every package whose `Version:` is built from macros (3 today).

### Defect accounting detail
- found 5 repo defects, all fixed and pushed this run: forbidden commit identity (9c4e375), logseq Release 2.0.2-2 with an unreleased file change (0260463), rootapp Release 0.9.156-1 with an unreleased file change (0260463), half-expanded version cells in the relay tool (4fe8d3d), stale "ten mains" prose in the prompt (4fe8d3d).
- The cliphist build fetches its Go modules over the network (`go: downloading go.etcd.io/bbolt v1.3.9` in COPR build log 11216187). That is the repo's Go convention (nwg-look builds the same way through `%gosource`), the module set is pinned by `go.sum`, and the build is green on all four chroots, so it is recorded here as a property, not a defect.

GAP: external - the scheduled run 40592518815 died because every free model in the cascade answered "Free usage limit reached" and the runner was then shut down (exit 137) before the checkpoint step could run; the free-tier quota is an OpenCode service limit that no repo change can lift, and the loss mode it exposed is answered by this run's checkpoint push at 05:40 (`86f68aa`).
GAP: external - ten commits already on main before this run are authored by `Qᴜɪᴇᴛᴄʀᴀꜰᴛ <mdzunaid384@gmail.com>` (`git log --format='%ae' origin/main | grep -c mdzunaid384` = 10). Whether that address is the owner's own web-identity or a stray agent config decides between preserving that authorship and normalising it, and a force-push that rewrites someone else's authorship cannot be undone, so it needs the owner's call. The tip commit was normalised and every commit this run created carries the allowed identity.

### Cross-reference and adversarial audit
- Official dist-git (`src.fedoraproject.org`): 5 of these names exist there (cliphist, python-yt-dlp-ejs, python-ytmusicapi, scenefx, wlroots). Each diff is deliberate: this repo keeps upstream floors where Fedora rawhide carries newer/older pins, and the astal/caelestia/mango stack has no Fedora package at all. No spec was changed to match dist-git: matching Fedora's pins is not a goal, building the newest upstream is.
- Terra cross-reference (`gh api repos/terra-*` specs fetched this run): for the 8 mains Terra also packages, our specs are at or ahead of Terra on every one (mangowm 0.18.3, greeter 1.7.0 vs our dbace1c nightly, helium 0.20.1.1, heroic 2.22.4, protonplus 0.6.8, zen 1.23.4 vs our 1.23.4b, umbriel and portal on the identical commit). Terra's umbriel spec carries `pkgconfig(md4c)`, which this repo's dependency re-derivation from the same source tree does not find and Terra's specs carry no `%check` for any of these six (this repo keeps its own where upstream has one).
- Fluxer hash pin (`# sha256: fb9d36c2…`): the pin is CORRECT. `sha256sum` of a complete 121,438,285-byte download of the `stable/linux/x64/latest/rpm` channel equals the pin, and `tools/hunt.py pins` independently hashed the same URL this run (0 mismatched, 0 unreachable). The earlier `FINDING fluxer.spec: pin mismatch ... got 1cd1405a` was a truncated read (curl rc 18) of the same URL - a receipt bug, fixed in `tools/hunt.py` (short read now raises) and `tools/fetch-sha256.sh` (never pins a partial body), plus a Range-resume downloader in `tools/teardown-sweep.py`.
- 11 of 63 packages ship no executable on purpose (libraries, fonts, icon themes, a lua binding, a lazy.nvim plugin tree): their probes are files-only, so their teardown token says `smoke SKIP-files-only` instead of claiming a smoke ran, and the verdict rests on install + `rpm -V` + the shipped file list.
- Install verdicts are read back from the container, never written from expectation: `rpm -V` clean, `ldd` over every entry point, then the per-package smoke from `tools/probes.txt`. A `PROBE-BUG` row would be a harness defect and is reported as such, not as a package failure.
- Host `rpmspec -P` expands bash-only macros with dash and shows empty `%{shortcommit}`/`%{tag}`; every spec-lint verdict above is from inside a Fedora container, which is the only authoritative expansion.
- OSV hits are filtered against each advisory's own `ranges` before a package is called affected, so `hunt: cves` counting 0 affected is a filtered result, not an unread one.

### Official packaging reference (this run)
- `git ls-remote https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/<pkg>.git HEAD` for all 63: 5 present (wlroots e479909c1df4, scenefx 7fb9afbf7466, cliphist f0f53f253faf, python-yt-dlp-ejs ee3eb4cfd666, python-ytmusicapi d0feb22582fd), 58 absent (no official spec to reconcile against).
- wlroots vs official rawhide spec 0.20.2-2: same BuildRequires set; ours differ only by the upstream version floors (`pkgconfig(egl) >= 1.5`, `pkgconfig(libseat) >= 0.2.0`, `pkgconfig(wayland-client) >= 1.24.0`); official's `gnupg2` is for its %gpgverify and `pkgconfig(x11-xcb)` is not declared by upstream 0.20.2 (`grep x11-xcb` over the extracted tree: no hit), so neither is adopted.

### Defects under repair
- mangowm 0.18.3-1: `mango.desktop` ships `Icon=mango` but the RPM installed no icon (upstream never installs `assets/mango.svg`), and `mango-portals.conf` routes ScreenCast/Screenshot to the wlr backend while the spec only recommended gtk. Fix in progress: install the icon, recommend xdg-desktop-portal-wlr.
- noctalia-greeter: `%check` calls `cmp` with no `diffutils` BuildRequires; the session script execs `dbus-run-session` (dbus-daemon) but the spec only required `dbus`, which on F44 pulls dbus-broker. Fix in progress.

### Toolchain (fedora:44 container, this run)

- `rpmspec -P` PASS: 65/65 specs expanded, 0 errors (`/tmp/spec-tools.log`: `RPMS PEC total=65 fail=0`).
- `dnf builddep` PASS: 65/65 specs resolved with ackerman/nexus enabled, 0 `no package matched` / `nothing provides` / `no match for argument` / `failed to solve` (`/tmp/dep-audit.log`: `DEP_SUMMARY ok=65 fail=0`).
- `rpmlint` PASS: 65 specfiles checked, 0 errors, 156 warnings, 0 badness (`/tmp/spec-tools.log`).
- `tools/teardown-sweep.py --type fedora` PASS: 65 packages torn apart, exit 0, `**Verdict: PASS** (0 failure(s))` -> `teardown-report.md`.
- `bash tools/check-workflows.sh` -> `WORKFLOW VALIDATION PASSED`; `bash tools/model-cascade.sh` starts `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`.
- `bash -n` on all 58 `update.sh` scripts: 0 syntax errors.

### Repairs landed this run

1. `hellwal` (commit f620000): 1.0.9 never reached any chroot. `Source: %{url}/archive/%{version}/...` pointed at a v-prefixed tag, so COPR build 11195380 failed all four chroots at the SRPM stage with `curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404`. Fixed with `%global tag v%{version}`, regenerated `hellwal.patch`, `%set_build_flags`, fish completion; `update.sh` now refuses a bump whose archive does not answer 200. New COPR build 11195791 succeeded on fedora-43/44/45/rawhide, and `hellwal-1.0.9-1.fc44.x86_64` installs PASS from the live repo.
2. `update-engine.yml` generator (commit 33ae1cb): the updater had no source-reachability gate, so the scanner/`update.sh` path could commit a 404 URL again. Added `tools/source-url-check.sh` plus a `Verify changed spec sources resolve` step that reverts a spec whose Source does not answer. Proved on a deliberately broken copy: `::warning::... archive/1.0.9/... (404)`, `unresolved=1`; the fixed spec gives `unresolved=0`.
3. `tools/hunt.py` (commit 006b35d): `hunt: builds` reported a count but never named the build that failed, so the receipt could not point at a log. It now prints the failing build id per package; tests `ALL PASS (12 cases)`; current output `hunt: builds - 65 packages, 0 failed`.
4. `opencode.json` + `tools/model-rank.txt` (commit 087f3a8): the default/general agent pointed at `minimax-m3.1-flash-free`, which the catalog no longer serves, and the new free model `big-pickle` was unranked. Repointed the defaults to `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, ranked `big-pickle` in tier 2 with its citation; the cascade no longer prints a NEW-model warning.
5. `tools/hunt.py` slice width (commit cb670d5): the rotation was computed as `ceil(n/8)` while `tools/verify-fedora.sh` requires `ceil(n/4)` per slice ("fleet rotates within 4 runs"). For a 65-package inventory the ledger could never satisfy the verifier: 9 named, 17 needed, and the verifier refused this run's first relay for exactly that. Width is now `ceil(n/4)`; this run then tore the 17 packages it names.
6. `tools/teardown-fresh.sh` (commit 0437890): `tools/probes.txt` marks a package with no smoke probe as `files-only` and `install-sweep.sh` honours that, but the teardown driver ran it as a command (`bash: files-only: command not found`, `SMOKE_EXIT=127`), turning a healthy package into a FAIL row. The sentinel is now read as "no probe"; proved by re-running `bibata-cursor-theme` with the literal sentinel -> `smoke SKIP-files-only`.
7. `teardown-report.md` (commit 0b29077): the committed receipt was stale - it still carried hellwal 1.0.8, craft-launcher 0.6.1, openchamber 2.5.0, an umbriel-git STALE row against a pin that has since moved, and `Verdict: FAIL`. ### Repairs this run
1. **obsidian was a release behind, and the release is a security fix** - upstream published 1.14.5 (2026-10-22T21:19Z) which updates Electron 43.7.5 -> 43.8.3; the spec pinned 1.14.4. Ran obsidian/update.sh, confirmed the .deb internally (`control`: `Version: 1.14.5`, sha256 c37fb46a966f604823337fb36ab23bd1baf8ce912ec35af59d62358a93357bee). COPR build 11194782 succeeded on all four chroots; obsidian-1.14.5-1 installs and smokes PASS on f44, f45 and f43.
2. **obsidian dropped an upstream runtime recommendation** - the .deb declares `Recommends: libappindicator3-1` (tray backend) and the spec carried no equivalent. Added `Recommends: libappindicator-gtk3` (verified present in F44 via mdapi: 12.10.1-10.fc44), same Release as fix 1, torn down and installed.
3. **umbriel-git was a nightly behind** - `git ls-remote noctalia-dev/umbriel HEAD` gave 6d57b5083ad7... against the pinned 36294ac3...; update.sh synced commit+gitdate, and the dependency block was re-derived from meson.build at the new commit (unchanged). COPR build 11194783 succeeded; umbriel-git-0.1.0^20261022212611git6d57b50-1 installs+smokes on f44 and rawhide and the published repodata carries it in all four chroots.
4. **tools/model-rank.txt ranked two models the catalog no longer serves** - `/inference/v1/models` on 2026-10-22 lists 8 free ids and neither minimax-m3.1-flash-free nor big-pickle is among them, so the cascade was silently thinning out. Dropped both, recorded the retirement in the file, and re-verified the chain.
5. **tools/model-cascade.sh dropped retired ids without saying so** - a ranked id the catalog stopped serving vanished from the chain silently, so the next run never learned to re-rank. It now prints `RETIRED FREE MODELS (catalog stopped serving them - drop them from tools/model-rank.txt): ...` on stderr. Proven by re-adding minimax-m3.1-flash-free: the announcement fires; with the file fixed it does not.
6. **tools/teardown-fresh.sh threw away double quotes in the smoke payload** - the payload was spliced into a `bash -lc` string, so `python3 -c 'import yt_dlp_plugins.extractor'` reached the container as `import` and exited with `SyntaxError: Expected one or more names after 'import'`. Four healthy python packages (python-yt-dlp-ejs, python-yt-dlp-get-pot, python-yt-dlp-get-pot-rustypipe, python-ytmusicapi) were reported smoke FAIL before that was caught. The payload now travels as a mounted file (`$OUTDIR/smoke.sh`, run as `bash /rpms/smoke.sh`), and all four were re-torn down: rpmbuild PASS, install PASS, smoke PASS.
7. **zig0.17 had no docker-teardown token in any relay** - it had never been built in a container, so its BuildRequires were only ever checked by `dnf builddep`. ### Repairs this run
1. **A killed runner lost 2h of verified work** - run 39772933169 printed `VERIFICATION PASSED` after 2h02m and was then killed (`The runner has received a shutdown signal`) with nothing pushed: issue #72. The scheduler now lands an on-disk relay checkpoint even when the agent dies (`Preserve relay checkpoint`, `if: always()`, one commit built from the relay blob) and the prompt tells the agent to keep the relay current while it works instead of writing it once at the end. Commit c330c20; `bash tools/check-workflows.sh` -> `WORKFLOW VALIDATION PASSED`; dry-run in a scratch clone committed as `opencode-agent[bot]`.
2. **wlroots pinned no `egl` floor** - meson asks `dependency('egl', version: '>= 1.5')`, the spec named a bare `pkgconfig(egl)`. Release 9 (commit 8dd1ac0), `pkgconfig(egl) >= 1.5`. COPR build 11194049 succeeded on fedora-43/44/45/rawhide and `wlroots-0.20.2-9` installs PASS in all four (install-test rows).
3. **nwg-look pinned no `golang` floor** - `go.mod` declares `go 1.26.0`, the spec named a bare `golang`. Release 2 (commit f1e549c), `golang >= 1.26`. The floor resolves in every chroot: golang 1.26.10 (f43, f44), 1.27.1 (f45), 1.27.3 (rawhide/f46), read from mdapi.fedoraproject.org and the f45 mirror listing this run.
4. **`tools/dep-floor-scan.py` could not see either of them** - it read meson trees only, so a Go toolchain floor was invisible (it printed `0 finding(s)` while nwg-look's floor was really missing), it discarded every plain `name >= ver` BuildRequires floor while parsing, and it accepted a BuildRequires that carried no floor at all. It now reads the `go` / `toolchain` directives of go.mod, parses plain floors, treats `1.26` == `1.26.0`, and takes `--tree pkg=dir` for a forge-macro Source0 that the host cannot expand; `--nofloor` (opt-in, because most specs here name a pc file bare) reports a dep the spec pins with no floor. `--selftest` PASS covers all of it, and against the pre-fix spec the scan prints `nwg-look NOFLOOR golang upstream=1.26.0 spec=-` where the fixed spec prints `0 finding(s)`.

### Repairs this run
1. **freebuff was one release behind (0.2.33 while upstream published 0.2.34).** `freebuff/update.sh` bumped Version, Release 1 and the Source0 sha256 to `5d9f18b5a56ac80e457547ca3859766a28fd8ddd32c396492f2cdb28b92507e2`, which an independent download confirmed. Fresh-container `rpmbuild -bb` + install + `rpm -V` + `freebuff --version` (prints 0.2.34) PASS; COPR build 11186533 succeeded in all four chroots; the published 0.2.34 installs and reports 0.2.34 on fedora-44 and fedora-45. Commit 6a58c64.
2. **rootapp moved to 0.9.153.** The rolling AppImage changed (content-length 497564152, last-modified 2026-10-22 07:17:55 GMT). `rootapp/update.sh` extracted 0.9.153 from inside the AppImage, not from a filename, and refreshed the sha256 to `a4a0d44fedf79fc4680d08b39f3bf4ebc79ef7a6ba305e8abf98a3d1efc34de1`. The squashfs magic probe now strips NUL bytes, so the updater stops printing a warning on every run. Fresh-container build + install + `rpm -V` + entry-point smoke + non-root Electron launch (rc 124, 0 `setuid_sandbox_host` lines) PASS; COPR build 11186616 succeeded in all four chroots and the published 0.9.153 installs on fedora-43, fedora-44 and fedora-45, with all four chroots serving 0.9.153-1 in the repodata. Commit 6c005c0.
3. **The fleet install probe was re-invented by every run, and a guessed path reported a healthy package as FAIL.** Twelve FAIL cells in the previous block were probe bugs, not broken packages: `concat --help` exits 1 on a GUI app whose real version probe is `concat --version`, and `/opt/fluxer/resources/app.asar` does not exist because fluxer installs to `/usr/lib64/fluxer/resources/app.asar`. New `tools/probes.txt` holds one probe per package (65 rows). `tools/install-sweep.sh` now skips comment lines, retries a package a mirror dropped mid-transaction, and reports a smoke that names a path the RPM does not ship as a `PROBE-BUG` row with the offending path instead of a package FAIL. `python3 tools/hunt.py probes` and a new `tools/verify-fedora.sh` check refuse a fleet without full probe coverage. Commit 9f89e99. Proof: the stale fluxer path produced `PROBE-BUG probe names /opt/fluxer/resources/app.asar which the RPM does not ship`, and the corrected probe produced PASS.
4. **A mirror failure during `dnf builddep` was reported as a package build failure.** protonplus failed with every BuildRequires listed as missing, because the dependency transaction itself failed; the same spec built and installed cleanly on the retry. `tools/teardown-fresh.sh` now retries builddep three times, prints the failing lines, and labels a pre-compile failure `FAIL builddep (dependencies unreachable, treat as repo/mirror)` instead of blaming the spec. Commit 533d900.

5. **teardown-report.md was a stale receipt.** It still carried freebuff 0.2.33 and rootapp 0.9.152 after both were bumped. `python3 tools/teardown-sweep.py --type fedora` re-tore all 65 packages from the current specs and rewrote it. It exited 0 with `=== TEAR-DOWN SWEEP PASSED`, and its rows read the internal versions from the artifacts themselves: freebuff `--version` 0.2.34, rootapp AppImage 0.9.153.

### Adversarial audit (why this could still be wrong, and what checked it)
1. All-green builds could hide a broken install, because COPR compiles but never installs. Attacked by installing all 65 published packages on fedora-43 and the ten mains on fedora-45 and rawhide; every row installed, `rpm -V` was clean and the probe ran.
2. The probe file could encode the same wrong assumption 65 times. Attacked by the new guard: the one deliberately stale path in the test (`/opt/fluxer/...`) came back `PROBE-BUG` with the path named, so a wrong probe cannot pass as a green row, and `hunt probes` plus the verifier refuse an inventory with no probe.
3. The two spec bumps could be "real change" churn. Attacked against git and COPR: neither 0.2.34 nor 0.9.153 was in `git log` or in any COPR build before this run, the sha256 of both artifacts was recomputed from a fresh download, and freebuff reports 0.2.34 from its own `--version`.
4. `dnf install` success could hide a sandbox-broken Electron app. Attacked with the AGENTS.md launch test on all ten Electron packages: rc 124 with 0 `setuid_sandbox_host` lines.
5. A transient mirror error could have been recorded as a package defect. Attacked by re-running every non-PASS row in a fresh container: all four passed (three were mirror skew on `libaom`, one was builddep), and the two generators were fixed so the next run reports them as mirror/probe problems.

### Repairs this run
1. **`ly` was pinned at 1.4.1 while upstream ships 1.5.0, and 1.5.0 could not be built with any Zig in the chroots.** `build.zig.zon` declares `.minimum_zig_version = "0.17.0"`; every chroot provides zig 0.16.0 (`dnf repoquery zig` in fedora:44/45/rawhide), and 0.16 fails on the 1.5.0 sources with `error: invalid builtin function: '@backingInt'`, `error: invalid builtin function: '@fromBackingInt'` and `error: no field named 'root' in struct 'Build'`. Fix, in two commits: `d929744` adds the `zig0.17` package (prebuilt upstream tarball, MIT, toolchain under `/usr/lib64/zig/0.17.0`, wrapper `/usr/bin/zig0.17`, so the distro zig 0.16 stays installable beside it) and `7a85690` moves ly to 1.5.0 built with it (`BuildRequires: zig0.17`, `--system zig-pkg`, `ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR`/`ZIG_LOCAL_CACHE_DIR` because 0.17 removed `--cache-dir`, refreshed PIE patch, `%check` proves the binary answers `--help`, `/etc/ly/example.lua` packaged). zig0.17 build 11185125 succeeded on all four chroots and is what every chroot publishes (`0.17.0-1.fc43`/`fc44`/`fc45`/`fc46`); ly build 11185136 succeeded on all four and publishes `1.5.0-1` (`dnf repoquery` after publish: `hunt.py` published-nvr reads `1.5.0-1` from all four chroots, 65 packages 0 findings).
2. **`ly` shipped an incomplete set of its bundled dependencies' license texts.** The 1.4.1 spec hand-listed 8 files (upstream `license.md`, zig-clap, zigini, ini, termbox2, aro, aro-UNICODE, translate-c) and missed the zlua module that `build.zig` imports, so a linked dependency shipped with no license text. The 1.5.0 spec installs every `LICENSE*`/`LICENCE`/`license`/`COPYRIGHT`/`COPYING` file the vendor bundle carries: the published `ly-1.5.0-1.fc44.x86_64` carries 10 files under `%{_licensedir}/ly`, zlua included, and the spec declares `Provides: bundled(zlua)`.
3. **`freebuff` was a release behind: 0.2.32 packaged, 0.2.33 published.** Proven from the artifact, not the filename: `./freebuff --version` on the 0.2.33 tarball prints `0.2.33` and its sha256 is `a01e8ecec7bfe4c895cf829131e7d853a5a3b092ded5ad6d3bbd7ed25b4bcbae`. `freebuff/update.sh` bumped Version, re-pinned the sha256 comment and added the 0.2.33 changelog entry; commit `1c8334a`, COPR build 11185184 succeeded (4/4 chroots), installed and smoke-tested from the live repo (`freebuff --version` -> 0.2.33).
4. **`tools/hunt.py` could not probe zig0.17** and emitted `UNPROBED-no-upstream-URL-and-no-vendor-feed`, so the newest package had no upstream evidence. `vendor_version()` now reads `https://ziglang.org/download/index.json` and compares the highest stable key with the spec pin (commit `3d27ceb`); the row now reads `upstream: zig0.17 0.17.0 == spec`.
5. **`tools/hunt.py` was blind to README rows for packages whose name carries a dot** (`^\| \`([a-z0-9-]+)\` \|` cannot match `zig0.17`), so the README check reported a missing row that was present. Pattern widened to `[a-z0-9.+-]+` (commit `102931c`); the check now reads 65 packages, 0 without a row.
6. **`tools/teardown-fresh.sh` treated a keep-alive GUI smoke as a failure and could not install a caller's extra packages.** An Electron/GUI smoke that stays alive returns 124, which the tool scored as `smoke FAIL`, and probes that need a helper package had no way to ask for it. Commit `5e597e1`: `SMOKE_EXIT=124` counts as PASS and `TD_EXTRAPKG` adds packages to the install container.
7. **README misdescribed which packages dnf can shadow.** It named `ly` as losing to Fedora's F45/Rawhide `1.5.0~rc1` (no longer true: the 1.5.0 final sorts above `~rc1`, `rpmdev-vercmp 1.5.0~rc1 1.5.0` -> `-1`) and missed the other shape entirely: Fedora's `python3-pydbus` carries `Provides: python-pydbus = 0.6.0-34.fc44`, so `dnf install python-pydbus` installs Fedora's build (`rpm -qa` after the install shows `python3-pydbus-0.6.0-34.fc44.noarch`), not this repo's licensed one. The note now names both shapes with the probe and the exact-NVR install, and the `python-pydbus` table row says the same.

   it). Commit 413f269 adds `vendor_index_latest()`: the spec's own Source0 host
   selects a vendor release index and the pinned major.minor bounds it, so
   zig0.17 now reads as newest from the index that ships the toolchain, a foreign
   host gets no answer, and nothing can be marked stale by a same-named project.

   "repology unreachable": Repology returns HTTP 200 with an empty list for
   zig0.17, so the receipt now says "repology has no entry" instead of blaming an
   outage.

Repairs in this execution:

1. `tools/teardown-batch.sh` wrote a verdict it never observed. It derived one `verdict` from the tool's exit code and printed it for all three stages, so a files-only package whose smoke was skipped was published as `smoke PASS`. Owned logs and the relay inherit that lie. Fixed: the token now transcribes the `TEARDOWN_<pkg>=` line the tool printed (`fields=${line#*=}`), and an empty line becomes an explicit three-stage FAIL. Before and after, driven by the same stub log (`TEARDOWN_pkg=... smoke SKIP-files-only`):
   - old: `docker-teardown: material-symbols-fonts rpmbuild-bb PASS install PASS smoke PASS | 2026-10-21`
   - new: `docker-teardown: material-symbols-fonts chroot:44 rpmbuild-bb PASS install PASS smoke SKIP-files-only | 2026-10-21`
2. `tools/teardown-fresh.sh` dropped the caller's extra packages on Electron packages: the Electron branch overwrote `EXTRAPKG` instead of extending it, so `TD_EXTRAPKG` was silently ignored exactly where a probe needs it (an X/GTK helper). Fixed to `util-linux xorg-x11-server-Xvfb ${TD_EXTRAPKG:-}`. Proven functionally, not by inspection: `TD_EXTRAPKG=cowsay tools/teardown-fresh.sh logseq 44 "cowsay -t ok" logseq` built logseq, installed it, ran the Electron non-root xvfb smoke and returned `smoke PASS`, `SANDBOX_FATAL=0`. With the old code cowsay is never installed, so the smoke would exit 127.
3. `materialyoucolor` was the only package with no `update.sh` and no path through the GitHub release scanner (its Source0 is a hashed `files.pythonhosted.org` sdist URL and its PyPI-only upstream has no GitHub releases). It would have gone stale with nothing in the pipeline to move it. Added `materialyoucolor/update.sh` following the PyPI updater pattern: reads `pypi.org/pypi/materialyoucolor/json`, exits 0 when the spec already matches, and on a real move rewrites the whole Source0 URL (the hash path is not derivable from the version), pins the sdist sha256 as a `# sha256:` comment, resets Release to 1 and rebuilds `%changelog` per repo policy. Both paths were executed: `-> [OK] Package is already at 3.0.4. No update needed.` exit 0 with a clean `git status`; in a scratch copy with Version forced to 3.0.3 it produced `Version: 3.0.4`, the correct hash-path Source0, the sha256 `30b8dde0...`, a single `3.0.4-1` changelog entry, and `rpmspec -P` rc 0. A second run on the bumped copy exits 0 (no churn). The push carrying the new updater triggered COPR build 11185324 for the package directory, and it succeeded on all four chroots (`build-chroot/list`: fedora-43, fedora-44, fedora-45, fedora-rawhide, all `succeeded`).

### Repairs this run
1. **umbriel-git was behind its own nightly upstream.** `gh api repos/noctalia-dev/umbriel/commits` returned HEAD eeb9aa2 while the spec pinned the previous snapshot. Commit 3bcf18c bumped commit/gitdate; COPR build 11184128 succeeded
   (`0.1.0^20261021170028giteeb9aa2-1`), and that NVR is what all four chroots publish (`repomd.xml` -> `primary.xml.gz` per chroot, parsed with an rpmvercmp comparison, not a string comparison).

Per the one-build-per-package-per-run rule the next run takes 8449975; re-bumping now would queue a second build for a package that is already green on all four chroots.
2. **`tools/teardown-fresh.sh` never ran the AGENTS.md Electron launch test.** heroic-games-launcher's first teardown this run reported `smoke FAIL` because the app died in Chromium's SUID-sandbox preflight (rc 133, `setuid_sandbox_host` FATAL) - the check could not see the very failure class the repo has an incident rule for. Commit 27db218 makes the tool detect `chrome-sandbox` in the spec and run the launch test with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` as a non-root user under xvfb (rc 0 or 124, `SANDBOX_FATAL=0`). After the fix the same package reports `SMOKE_EXIT=124`, `SANDBOX_FATAL=0`, teardown PASS, and non-Electron packages are unchanged (mangowm, ly, wlroots re-run PASS).

### Gaps
GAP: external - ly 1.5.0 cannot be packaged with the zig the distro ships: fedora-43/44/45/rawhide all carry zig 0.16.0, and ly v1.5.0's build.zig targets zig 0.17 APIs. Probe this run: with 1.5.0 checked out and `minimum_zig_version` relaxed, `zig build` fails with `error: invalid builtin function: '@backingInt'` and `error: no field named 'root' in struct 'Build'`. 1.4.1 is therefore the newest ly this repo can publish; the package itself is healthy (published 1.4.1-5 on all four chroots, installed and smoke-tested twice this run).

### The zen-browser withdrawal, corrected end to end (this run)
1. Upstream published `1.23.4b` and withdrew it within minutes. Probes run this run: `gh api repos/zen-browser/desktop/releases/latest` -> `1.23.3b`; `.../releases/tag/1.23.4b` -> HTTP 404; `.../contents/?ref=1.23.4b` -> "No commit found for the ref". The spec had already been bumped to `1.23.4b` and build 11182544 had shipped it to all four chroots, so the repo was serving a version upstream no longer has.
2. Revert to `1.23.3b`: commit 92e5b1a.
3. A plain revert would NOT have shipped: the published NVR was `1:1.23.4b-1` and `1.23.3b-4 < 1.23.4b`, so `dnf install zen-browser` would keep resolving to the withdrawn build. Fix: `Epoch: 2` (commit 9cbd328). Build 11182728 succeeded, and all four chroots' `primary.xml.gz` now carry `2:1.23.3b-4` (probe: `repomd.xml` -> `data type="primary"` href -> gunzip -> `<version epoch="2" ver="1.23.3b" rel="4.fc<NN>">`), so a fresh `dnf install` picks `1.23.3b-4` (pasted in the install-test table).

### mangowm dependency defect, fixed
`meson.build:104` calls `find_program('find')` with no `required: false`; no BuildRequires provided it, so the build succeeded only because the COPR chroot image happens to carry `findutils`. Fixed in commit 1aac137 (`BuildRequires: findutils`, Release 1 -> 2), shipped as build 11182680 (`0.18.2-2`, four chroots succeeded), installed and smoke-tested from the live repo.

### Changed, defects and gaps (this run)
changed: zen-browser mangowm
defects-found: 4
defects-fixed: 3

1. zen-browser shipped `1.23.4b`, a version upstream withdrew within minutes (release page 404, tag 404, no commit for the ref). FIXED, 92e5b1a.
2. The published `1:1.23.4b-1` still outranked a plain revert, so users would never get `1.23.3b` back. FIXED with `Epoch: 2`, 9cbd328; build 11182728 succeeded on all four chroots and every chroot's repodata now serves `2:1.23.3b-4`.
3. mangowm called `find_program('find')` at meson.build:104 with no BuildRequires providing it. FIXED, 1aac137 (`BuildRequires: findutils`, Release 2); build 11182680 succeeded.
4. ly is one release behind: upstream 1.5.0 requires zig 0.17.0, and every chroot ships zig 0.16.0 (`dnf repoquery --repo=fedora-44 zig` -> 0.16.0; upstream `build.zig.zon` `minimum_zig_version` -> 0.17.0). External.

GAP: external - ly 1.5.0 needs zig 0.17.0 and no enabled chroot (fedora-43/44/45/rawhide as of 2026-10-21) ships it yet; the repo stays on 1.4.1-5, which builds and installs clean (teardown + install-test above).

Also re-checked and NOT defects, with the probe that cleared each: astal specs' `g-ir-compiler` resolves transitively (`dnf builddep` on astal-io pulls `gobject-introspection-devel`); `xcb-render`/`xcb-xfixes` come from `libxcb-devel` via `pkgconfig(xcb)`; `wayland-egl` ships in `wayland-devel`; protonplus' `desktop-file-validate`/`appstreamcli`/`appstream-util`/`glib-compile-schemas` come from `desktop-file-utils`/`appstream`/`libappstream-glib`/`glib2`.

#### Maintenance session (human-driven, 2026-10-20) - the contract was measuring strings

A human session audited the last runs instead of trusting the green ticks. Run
39415197314 published an install-test table whose 34 verdict cells said FAIL
while its own prose said "47 rows, all PASS" - and 24 of those same packages
carried a same-run `docker-teardown: ... install PASS`. Only 1 of the 47 NVRs
was missing from the live repodata, so those FAILs were written, not observed.

ROOT CAUSE of the under-acting maintainer: the gate and the verifier grepped
for the PRESENCE of evidence strings, never their truth. A run that produced 64
greppable rows and wrote "status: complete" was cheaper than a run that fixed
one thing, so that is what the agent produced - every run for days. Nothing
counted repairs, so hunting for defects had no payoff in the contract. The
authority clause ("do not ask permission, you already have it") was prose, and
prose is not enforced.

FIXED IN CODE (this commit): the gate and tools/verify-fedora.sh now parse the
install-test table - any verdict that is not PASS fails the run unless it is
EXTERNAL with a matching GAP: external line, and a FAIL cell next to a
same-run docker-teardown install PASS is a contradiction that fails the run.
Every run must carry `defects-found: N` and `defects-fixed: M` (the gate
computes M + external_gaps >= N) and at least 5 distinct `hunt:` category
lines. A verdict is now a transcript of a command, never a summary.

ALSO: the free-model cascade is derived from the live catalog at run time
(tools/model-cascade.sh) with the strength order in tools/model-rank.txt, so
the strongest free model goes first and a model the catalog drops stops
costing attempt slots. The comment policy (short topic labels only) and the
root-cause note are in AGENTS.md for the next run.

- Why this class was worth 21 commits: the specs declared a license and installed **no license text at all** - 21 of 64 packages. Fedora review rejects that, and `%license` is also what puts the text in the source RPM. The fix is mechanical and verifiable (file present in the built RPM and in every published chroot), not a cosmetic release bump.
- `freebuff` also carried a wrong declaration: `License: Apache-2.0` against a repository whose LICENSE (and the GitHub license API) say **MIT**, with zero Apache-2.0 strings in the shipped binary and 10 embedded `MIT License` strings. Corrected with that evidence, not by preference.
- Two packages are deliberately NOT in the class: `obsidian` and `rootapp` are `LicenseRef-Proprietary` and ship no redistributable license text - the declaration is the whole licence statement, and inventing a text file would be worse than shipping none.

#### Defects found and fixed this run (each committed and pushed separately)
- **localsend 1.18.2-2 -> 1.18.2-3**: commit 794ee38 corrected `License: GPL-3.0` to `Apache-2.0` but left Release at 2. COPR rebuilt the identical NVR (11171205) and a clean fedora:44 container running `dnf upgrade localsend` printed `Nothing to do.` - the corrected metadata could never reach installed users. After the bump: build 11171283 succeeded, live-repo install yields `localsend-1.18.2-3.fc44 LICENSE=Apache-2.0`.
- **obsidian 1.14.4-1 -> 1.14.4-2**: same defect with `Commercial` -> `LicenseRef-Proprietary` (794ee38). New build 11171384 -> live install `obsidian-1.14.4-2.fc44 LICENSE=LicenseRef-Proprietary`.
- **rootapp 0.9.148-1 -> 0.9.148-2**: same defect with `Proprietary` -> `LicenseRef-Proprietary` (794ee38). New build 11171385 -> live install `rootapp-0.9.148-2.fc44 LICENSE=LicenseRef-Proprietary`.
- **fluxer 2026.1018.223338-1 -> -2**: the spec advertised `AGPL-3.0-or-later AND BSD`. Bare `BSD` is not an SPDX identifier and is absent from Fedora's `fedora-spdx-licenses.toml` (629 lines / 623 ids; BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, BSD-4-Clause are present). Downloaded the pinned artifact (sha256 de3c4e3c... matches the spec pin), read `app.asar` package.json (`AGPL-3.0-or-later`) and all bundled npm license declarations (MIT, ISC, 0BSD, Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause) plus `LICENSES.chromium.html` (BSD-2/3-Clause, IJG, Openssl, MPL-1.1, GPL/LGPL family; chromium.spec is Fedora's reference wording). New build 11171455 -> live install carries the corrected expression. rpmlint on the built RPM raises no `invalid-license`.
- **ly HOLD re-proven**: upstream v1.5.0's `build.zig.zon` sets `minimum_zig_version = "0.17.0"`; Fedora 43/44/45/rawhide all ship zig 0.16.0 - external blocker, spec stays 1.4.1-5, no churn.
- **No other spec was touched**: 60 of 64 packages matched upstream exactly, so pushing a rebuild would have shipped nothing (same-NVR republish is churn).

#### Probe-bug corrections (each started as a red probe, proven a probe bug, not a package bug)

  `umbriel-git` (`rpm -q` matches names, not Provides). Re-probe:
  `rpm -q umbriel-git` -> installed, RPMV_EXIT=0.
- `pkg-config --modversion wlroots` exited 1 because wlroots 0.20 ships the
  versioned file `wlroots-0.20.pc` (mangowm BuildRequires
  `pkgconfig(wlroots-0.20)`). Re-probe `pkg-config --modversion wlroots-0.20`
  -> 0.20.2, rc 0.
- `nwg-look --version` exited 2: it is a Go binary with single-dash flags
  (`-v display Version information`). Re-probe `nwg-look -v` -> "nwg-look
  version 1.2.1", rc 0.
- `rpmbuild -bb` exiting 11 on the python packages is the
  %generate_buildrequires two-pass flow (it writes
  `*.buildreqs.nosrc.rpm` and stops), not a broken spec: install the
  generated buildreqs and rebuild. COPR/mock does this automatically.

#### Churn audit of auto-updater commits + generator fix (IMPROVE THE MACHINE, 2026-10-18)
- Audit method: shallow clone deepened to 205 commits; every `github-actions[bot]` commit since 2026-10-11 inspected; each `Version:`/-/+ pair across all `.spec` hunks extracted (14 bot commits, ~30 version moves).
- Result: **2 real downgrades found** (all other moves were forward): zen-browser `64da796` (2026-10-16 10:18Z) moved 1.23.3b -> 1.23.2b, restored by `cf40866` next run; fluxer `b0b7392` (2026-10-11 21:11Z) moved 2026.1010.155917 -> 2026.1006.171735, restored by `2c7ea42`. Each cost a wasted COPR rebuild of an older tarball plus a second rebuild to come back.
- Root cause (generator, not symptom): every updater compares with plain `!=` ("different = update"), so a transient upstream state reads as a newer version. Evidence for the transients: zen's `releases/latest` shows 1.23.3b created 2026-10-16T16:23Z / published 22:08Z — upstream's release workflow deletes assets while re-running (noted in zen's own update.sh), so `git ls-remote` at 10:18Z saw 1.23.2b as newest; fluxer's rolling download URL served its 10-06 artifact after we shipped the 10-10 build.
- FIX PUSHED `45c1e8a`: new workflow step `Guard against version downgrades` in `.github/workflows/update-engine.yml`, placed between the scanner and `Check for Changes` — a single choke point covering all 56 update.sh scripts AND the GitHub-API scanner without touching any package. Reverts any spec whose `Version:` (or literal `%global tag`, v-prefix stripped; macro tags excluded, wlroots computes tag from %{version}) moved backwards, emits `::warning::`, `downgrades-reverted=N` to the log, exits 0.
- Guard verified by simulation on a scratch clone (extracted step source via PyYAML and ran it): (1) zen incident 1.23.3b->1.23.2b BLOCKED+reverted; (2) fluxer incident BLOCKED+reverted; (3) legit upgrade starship 1.26.0->1.27.0 passes; (4) tag-driven protonplus `v0.6.8 -> v0.6.7` BLOCKED+reverted; (5) tag upgrade `v0.6.8 -> v0.6.9` passes. Also unit-tested `sort -V` ordering on 10 version pairs incl. 1.23.2b->1.23.10b and 2026.40.1->2026.41.
- Workflow checks re-run after the edit: YAML-OK all 3 workflows, permission-keys-OK (update-engine: contents+issues), no other workflow contains the `latest_ver != current_ver` comparison bug. `actionlint` unavailable (named gap above).
- Zero churn confirmed elsewhere: umbriel-git's two auto-updates were genuine pin refreshes (commit SHA + gitdate changed in Source each time), no no-op commits; no `update.sh` had left a spec headerless (guard intact).

### Install-sweep failure found and fixed by this continuation: zen-browser on fedora-45 (commit 0bbea1d, Release 1 -> 2, COPR build 11166534 succeeded 07:57:51Z)

- BEFORE (07:25Z, clean fedora:45 container, live ackerman/nexus repo): `dnf install zen-browser` printed `nothing provides libnssutil3.so(NSSUTIL_3.130)(64bit) needed by zen-browser-1:1.23.3b-1.fc45.x86_64 from copr:copr.fedorainfracloud.org:ackerman:nexus`, then exited 0 by silently falling back to the stale `zen-browser-1.23.2b-1.fc45` still in the repodata. `rpm -q zen-browser` in that test printed 1.23.2b-1, not 1.23.3b-1, so Fedora 45 users never received the current browser.
- LIVE AFTER (08:00Z, clean fedora:45 container, published repodata, the test a user runs): `LIVE_INSTALL_EXIT=0`, `Complete!`, `NVR=zen-browser-1:1.23.3b-2.fc45.x86_64`, `LIVE_RPMV_EXIT=0`, `LIVE_SMOKE=Mozilla Zen 1.23.3b`, `NSSUTIL_REQ_COUNT=0`.
- Cause, proven by extraction instead of guessed: the binary RPM holds **zero ELF files outside `/opt/zen`** (`find . -type f -not -path './opt/*' | xargs file | grep -c ELF` -> 0), and `readelf -V` hits for `NSSUTIL_3.130` are only `./opt/zen/libnssutil3.so`, `./opt/zen/libnss3.so` and `./opt/zen/libsmime3.so`, all three shipped inside the package. RPM auto-generates Requires from those bundled copies, so Zen's private NSS demanded `libnssutil3.so(NSSUTIL_3.130)` from the distro. Fedora 45 ships `nss-util 3.129.0-1.fc45` (stops at NSSUTIL_3.129), Fedora 44 carries `nss-util 3.131.0-1.fc44` and resolved by luck, which is why only the newer chroot broke.
- Fix: add `nssutil3|nss3|smime3|nspr4` to the spec's existing `__requires_exclude`, the rule the spec comment already states (internal-only bundled libraries must not become system Requires, gtk/X11/wayland stays auto-generated). Release 1 -> 2 plus a %changelog entry. Commit 0bbea1d.
- AFTER in the harness (fresh fedora:45 and fedora:44 containers, 07:45-07:52Z): `rpmspec -P` EXIT=0, `spectool -g` EXIT=0, `dnf builddep` EXIT=0 with 0 unresolved markers, `rpmbuild -bb` -> `zen-browser-1.23.3b-2.fc45` and `.fc44`, NSS require count **0**, system requires kept (111 total, 4 gtk/wayland/X11), `dnf install` EXIT=0 `Complete!`, `rpm -V` EXIT=0, `zen --version` rc=0 printing `Mozilla Zen 1.23.3b`, bundled `libnssutil3.so` ldd resolves with 0 missing libs.
- No-regression check: the 6 libs `ldd /opt/zen/libxul.so` reports as not found are `libmozsandbox libgkcodecs liblgpllibs libmozsqlite3 libmozgtk libmozwayland`, all already in `__requires_exclude` before this change and identical for the pre-existing packaging, so this edit dropped no system dependency that was previously satisfied.
- rpmlint PASS: zen-browser (0 errors, 2 warnings `no-%check-section` / `no-%build-section`, expected for a binary repack; container run `RPMLINT_EXIT=0`).

ly fedora-45 correction (A3 finding, verified and documented): the first ly@45 run installed `ly-1.5.0~rc1-1.fc45` from Fedora's `updates-testing`, NOT our package - `rpm -q ly` still succeeded, so the old marker-based log read PASS while testing Fedora's rpm. Re-run twice: (a) fedora:43 natural `dnf install ly` -> `ly-1.4.1-5.fc43` from our COPR (Fedora f43 only ships 1.4.0), rpm -V clean, smoke rc=0; (b) fedora:45 with `--disablerepo=updates-testing` -> `ly-1.4.1-5.fc45` from our COPR, rpm -V clean, smoke rc=0 (`/tmp/itr/ly-43-natural.log`, `/tmp/itr/ly-45-copr-only.log`). The ly secondary row is therefore re-scoped to fedora-43 above. This is packaging reality, not a defect in our spec: on F45 Fedora's own newer EVR wins `dnf install ly` while `updates-testing` carries the rc - expected dnf behaviour, recorded here so the row cannot be read as proof about our F45 rpm. Our ly 1.4.1 remains the newest packageable version (v1.5.0 held: build.zig.zon `minimum_zig_version = 0.17.0`, and `zig 0.16.0` installed in fresh fedora:43/44/45/rawhide containers today).

### Harness learnings (repo untouched, /tmp only)
- dynamic-BR specs need mock-parity loop: rpmbuild -bb -> dnf builddep <buildreqs rpm> -> repeat (mprisify took 3 iters: static, then packaging/pip/setuptools, then pygobject+pydbus). Single-pass FAIL is a harness bug, never a package bug.
- `echo $?` after a pipe reports the last command; redirect to file first, then read.
- sed on captured output cannot fix placeholders inside the container command; pass PKG via docker -e.
- fixed ~/.config/copr being a mode-600 directory (config-file path blocked); rewrote as file, copr-cli whoami OK.

### Pattern fix (execution 2): pipefail/SIGPIPE race in the completion gates
Found while re-running the verifier: `tools/verify-fedora.sh` main/slice checks used `echo "$scope" | grep -q ...` under `set -o pipefail`. grep -q exits at the first match, the write side takes SIGPIPE, the pipeline returns 141, and a passing check reads as FAIL - reproduced 9/20 false failures on identical input once this run's relay grew past the pipe buffer. This is a broken check, not broken evidence, so the check got fixed, not bypassed:
- tools/verify-fedora.sh: 3 early-exit pipes -> here-string greps (`grep -qE ... <<< "$scope"`), same patterns, same strictness. After the fix: 5/5 verifier runs exit 0, output identical across runs.
- .github/workflows/opencode-schedule.yml gate_passes(): 10 `printf ... | grep -q ... || return 1` lines converted to here-strings + `slice_line=$(grep -m1 ... <<< "$content" || true)`. Same race existed under GitHub's implicit `shell: bash` (-eo pipefail).

### Improvement landed (2026-10-24)
- `tools/hunt.py`: new `chroot-docs` category. It compares the chroots COPR actually builds (`chroot_repos`) with the releases README promises, both directions, plus a check that no enabled chroot is older than the oldest supported Fedora. Output: `hunt: chroot-docs - 4 chroots vs README [43,44,45+rawhide], 0 findings`.
- `tools/test-hunt-helpers.py`: positive and negative cases (undocumented chroot, phantom release, rawhide drift, missing README line) prove the new check can fail: `PASS: hunt chroot-docs helpers (4 readme cases)`.
- `AGENTS.md`: tools list names the new category, so the next run knows it exists.
- Payoff: Fedora rotates twice a year. Before this, README could promise a release no chroot builds (or hide a chroot users cannot see) and every hunt still reported clean. Now the documentation claim and the build matrix are checked against each other every run.
- Registry of this run: `python3 tools/test-sweep-helpers.py` -> ALL PASS (12 cases); `python3 -m py_compile tools/hunt.py` -> OK; `python3 tools/hunt.py probes` -> 63 rows, 63 specs, 0 findings.
